Utility or helper functions that are not part of the public `mermaidAPI` interface should not reside in `mermaidAPI.ts`; flag these for relocation to more appropriate modules so that `mermaidAPI.ts` stays focused on the public API surface.

When a pre-release (e.g. alpha) version of the package is published to npm specifically to allow testing of a PR, include the npm package URL in the PR description so reviewers and external testers can easily install and validate the changes.

When adding properties or methods to interfaces in `packages/mermaid/src/diagram-api/types.ts` (e.g. `DiagramRenderer`, `DiagramDefinition`), verify that each addition is placed in the interface whose responsibility it best matches — for example, a method that extracts style class definitions has a stronger affinity with styling concerns than with rendering concerns.
